definition: The ability of an atom to attract the shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond towards itself; data booklet values run from 0.7 up to 4.0 for fluorine.
Uneven sharing of the electron pair in a covalent bond, caused by a difference in electronegativity between the two bonded atoms.
A charge smaller than a full ionic charge, written $\delta^{+}$ or $\delta^{-}$, on an atom at either end of a polar bond.
A measure of charge separation, the partial charges multiplied by the distance between them, that also has a direction, so bond dipoles add as vectors.
A molecule with a net dipole moment, because it has polar bonds arranged so that their bond dipoles do not cancel.
